consensus:
Nine references, weighted hard toward the three that share the target's shape: uRU9SzlVClg and -dHfHZgtXJw (locked-off stream captures cut between discrete crop windows on one continuous source) and 8cO8UWyjGyc (two subjects inside one source frame, alternating fixed crops). The recipe those three agree on, in ten lines:
1. Everything is one continuous source. All cuts in all three are same-scene reframes (same_scene_reframe_pct = 100 on each). Nothing cuts away.
2. Only 2-4 crop rectangles are ever used, they are saved and reused exactly (8cO8UWyjGyc returns to a window within 1 px and 0.05% scale), and switching between them is an instant hard cut, never an animated push.
3. Cut every ~1.8 s, ~30 cuts/min (uRU9SzlVClg 31.5, 8cO8UWyjGyc 36.1, -dHfHZgtXJw 24.7). Shots run 0.5-3.6 s.
4. Cuts land on speech events - onsets, boundaries, speaker changes, pauses - not on a metronome (8cO8UWyjGyc, _LQ379ZhspI, 9L2Yrs6jwb4, uRU9SzlVClg).
5. Framing follows the voice: reframe to whoever/whatever is being talked about (8cO8UWyjGyc alternates kid/Kai across the exchange).
6. The crop is frozen inside a shot: uRU9SzlVClg measures s=1.0000, |dx|,|dy| < 0.4 px for 17 s; -dHfHZgtXJw -0.23 to +1.13 %/s; _LQ379ZhspI pixel-static. No shake anywhere in any of the nine that is not the source's own handheld camera.
7. Captions are 1-2 all-caps words per card, ~0.4 s each, running essentially continuously (96.4% of frames on uRU9SzlVClg), in a heavy condensed grotesque at 6-7.5% of frame height.
8. Each card enters with a centre-anchored scale pop: 0.85-0.91 -> peak ~1.05 at +83 ms -> 1.00 by ~130 ms. Three clips, no averaging needed - they agree.
9. Editor-added effects are near zero. uRU9SzlVClg and 8cO8UWyjGyc have literally none. Flashes, glows and grades belong to the other six.
10. Hook is verbal, not visual: open cold mid-sentence, caption already burnt in on frame 1, first cut inside 0.9 s, and put the clip's shortest shot in the first 1.2 s. No title card exists in any of the nine.

framing_ladder: WIDE   f=1.00  -> crop 608x1080 - the full-height 9:16 window. Backed by -dHfHZgtXJw shots 8-11 (measured base, several later shots return to it at s=1.0003-1.0014) and 8cO8UWyjGyc's widest framing held at 6.70s.
MEDIUM f=0.88  -> crop 536x950  - reconciles -dHfHZgtXJw's 1.10-1.13x (=1/1.10..1/1.13 = 0.885-0.909, 388 and 158 ORB inliers) with 8cO8UWyjGyc's 1.15x (=0.870).

TIGHT  f=0.76  -> crop 462x820  - 8cO8UWyjGyc measures this one directly rather than as a ratio: its two working windows sit at scale 0.755 and 0.758 in units of the wide crop, i.e. crop factor 0.755-0.758, and it also states them as 1.32-1.34x. -dHfHZgtXJw shot 7 lands here too (1.21-1.32x = 0.76-0.83) but that clip flags it as +/-10% uncertain because the rotating prize wheel contaminates ORB.
PUNCH  f=0.71  -> crop 432x766  - -dHfHZgtXJw shots 1-3 at ~1.40x (=0.714) and 8cO8UWyjGyc's tight end at 1.38x (=0.725). This is the tightest level the two ladder-measuring clips share.

(optional) EXTREME f=0.67 -> crop 408x724 - one clip only: _LQ379ZhspI's BEAST-TIGHT is ~1.5x its BEAST-WIDE, established from subject measurement (head 31-39% of frame height wide vs 51-55% tight) after ORB gave a false match. Do not use as a default rung.

COORDINATE NOTE: f is the crop factor relative to the widest 9:16 window of a 1920x1080 frame (608x1080 = 1.00); smaller f = tighter. Both source ladders were published as zoom factors (larger = tighter) and are inverted here. Rectangles are round-to-even of 608*f and 1080*f, which drifts the aspect by <=0.2% (462/820 = 0.5634 vs 0.5625) - harmless once scaled to 1080x1920, but keep both dimensions even for H.264.

LADDER SIZE: use 3 rungs by default. -dHfHZgtXJw lists 4 zoom levels across 8 distinct framings; 8cO8UWyjGyc uses 3-4; uRU9SzlVClg uses only 2 for the whole clip and is still the closest structural analogue to the target.
shot_grammar.reframe_vs_cutaway_ratio: 100:0. All three target-relevant clips measure same_scene_reframe_pct = 100 (uRU9SzlVClg, -dHfHZgtXJw, 8cO8UWyjGyc). The renderer cannot cut away in one pass anyway, so this costs nothing. For contrast, the less relevant six run 0 (Cfpc04Tpc4k), 6.7 (q-SaGj-pDh0), 20 (_LQ379ZhspI), 50 (8-eCvn1gWIg), 66.7 (9L2Yrs6jwb4) - and every one of those cutaways needs footage the renderer does not have.
rules: CUT ON SPEECH ONSET. 8cO8UWyjGyc: 'cuts land on speech boundaries' and the audio runs continuously across every cut. _LQ379ZhspI measures mean level rise 11.5 dB at its 10 cut points vs 6.9 dB (sd 4.9) at 129 random non-cut times - about 0.9 sd, i.e. cuts sit on onsets and carry no added whoosh. Signal: cut at the first frame of a speech onset whose RMS rise exceeds the local p90.

CUT ON SPEAKER CHANGE, BUT NOT EVERY ONE. 9L2Yrs6jwb4: all 3 cuts land exactly on a speaker change, but only 3 of the 6 speaker turns get a cut. Signal: speaker change is a candidate, gated by min_shot_s - take it only if the current shot has run >= 0.6 s.

CUT ON A PAUSE. uRU9SzlVClg's 14.517 s cut is confirmed by a 167 ms audio silence gap straddling it (-47.9 dB RMS). -dHfHZgtXJw ducks to -54.8 dBFS into the 15.117 s cut. Signal: any speech gap >= 150 ms is a free cut point.

FRAMING FOLLOWS THE VOICE, NOT THE PICTURE. 8cO8UWyjGyc alternates its two windows across a question-and-reaction exchange; a yellow (kid) caption runs over a Kai shot at 3.72-4.25 s, so the colour tracks the speaker while the crop tracks the beat. For the target: switch to the facecam window on the speaker's own speech, to the gameplay window on the thing being described.

GO TIGHTER ON ENERGY, WIDER ON THE PAYOFF. -dHfHZgtXJw opens at its tightest rung (~1.40x, f=0.71) mid-shout with audio at its loudest of the whole clip (-6.8 dBFS RMS in the first 100 ms) and settles to f=1.00 for the calmer middle (shots 8-11). 8cO8UWyjGyc holds its widest framing for the 4.93 s payoff at the end. Signal: map the framing rung to windowed speech RMS percentile, with the tightest rung reserved for the top decile.

DO NOT SPEND A SHOT ON A DEAD REGION. Not measurable from the nine (none contains gameplay), but structurally implied by 8cO8UWyjGyc's rule that every window contains a subject. Keep the existing game_dead_below motion gate.

FRONT-LOAD THE SHORTEST SHOT. uRU9SzlVClg's first shot (0.65 s) is the shortest in the clip. 8cO8UWyjGyc's shortest shot (0.317 s, the Kai reaction at 0.867-1.183 s) sits entirely inside the first 1.2 s. Signal: allow min_shot_s to halve for the first 1.5 s.

FIRST CUT INSIDE 0.9 s. -dHfHZgtXJw 0.350 s, uRU9SzlVClg 0.650 s, 8cO8UWyjGyc 0.867 s. The less relevant clips run later (Cfpc04Tpc4k 1.101, 8-eCvn1gWIg 1.400, 9L2Yrs6jwb4 2.250, _LQ379ZhspI 2.400, q-SaGj-pDh0 2.833), so this rule is target-weighted, not a nine-clip consensus.

REUSE RECTANGLES EXACTLY. 8cO8UWyjGyc's KAI window returns to within 1 px and 0.05% scale after cutting away and back; -dHfHZgtXJw's framing returns to exact identity seconds apart (shot 8 vs shot 11 s=0.9996, rot=+0.026 deg). Compute each camera rect once per clip and re-emit the identical numbers, never recompute per shot.
HOLD THE CROP STILL INSIDE A SHOT. See effect_spec; this is a rule, not a taste call - three of the four locked-off references measure zero ramp.

caption_spec.font_family: Heavy condensed all-caps grotesque, Anton/Impact class. NOT IDENTIFIED by any profile - 8cO8UWyjGyc, _LQ379ZhspI and 8-eCvn1gWIg each list the exact typeface under 'could not determine'. Treat Anton as a substitute, not a measurement.
caption_spec.cap_height_evidence: 8cO8UWyjGyc 7.55% (145 px at 1920), -dHfHZgtXJw 7-8% glyph height (100-120 px at 1440), uRU9SzlVClg 5.8% (111 px). Wider set for context: _LQ379ZhspI 6.8%, 9L2Yrs6jwb4 5.2%, 8-eCvn1gWIg 4.4%, q-SaGj-pDh0 4.0%. 7.0% is the centre of the two target-relevant measurements; uRU9SzlVClg gets away with 5.8% because it sits on an opaque card.
caption_spec.vertical_position_evidence: Taken from 8cO8UWyjGyc, the only reference with two subjects inside one source frame, which is the target's structure. There it puts the text centre at 62.5% with the two faces at 21-24% and 32-35%, i.e. deliberately clear of both. The other two target-relevant clips disagree sharply (uRU9SzlVClg 73.5%, -dHfHZgtXJw 50.0%) - see disagreements.
caption_spec.vertical_position_rule: Place the text centre in the largest vertical band that contains neither the facecam subject's head box nor the top of the game HUD, clamped to 55-75% of frame height. Every one of the seven captioned references sits below mid-frame (50.0, 50.2, 51.1, 52.9, 62.5, 73.5, 77.9) and none is near the 43% the old recipe claimed.
caption_spec.horizontal_position: Centred. Measured dead-centre in every captioned clip: uRU9SzlVClg bbox centre x = 540/1080 exactly; -dHfHZgtXJw 48.9-50.7% of width; 9L2Yrs6jwb4 cx 534-543 of 1080; _LQ379ZhspI 50.0%; q-SaGj-pDh0 cx 547.5 vs 540.

words_per_card.evidence: uRU9SzlVClg 1.6, _LQ379ZhspI 1.4, 8cO8UWyjGyc 1.33, -dHfHZgtXJw 1.2, 9L2Yrs6jwb4 1.0. Six of seven captioned clips fall in 1.0-1.9; the only outlier is q-SaGj-pDh0 at 3.5, a handheld selfie vlog that builds multi-word cards word by word. Note all of these are read counts off contact sheets, not OCR - uRU9SzlVClg counted 45 words over 29 legible cards of 40, _LQ379ZhspI 46 of 77, -dHfHZgtXJw ~28 cards, q-SaGj-pDh0 by eye.

card_duration_s.evidence: 8cO8UWyjGyc 15 cards over 6.70 s = 0.45 s mean; uRU9SzlVClg 40 cards over 17.1 s = 0.43 s; 9L2Yrs6jwb4 22 cards over 10.25 s = 0.47 s; _LQ379ZhspI 77 cards over 27.4 s = 0.36 s mean with card gaps p10/p50/p90 = 0.15/0.30/0.65 s. -dHfHZgtXJw runs shortest, most cards 0.10-0.40 s.

caption_spec.screen_coverage: Near-continuous. uRU9SzlVClg has captions up in 991/1028 frames (96.4%); _LQ379ZhspI in 273 of 274 sampled frames. Do not leave the frame textless during speech.

color_rule.multi_speaker: One saturated colour per speaker, assigned by WHO IS SPEAKING and not by who is on screen. This is the strongest cross-clip finding in the set: all four references with 2+ speakers do it and each carries a decisive off-screen proof - 8cO8UWyjGyc (yellow #FDF400 kid / near-white #F1F6FB Kai; a yellow card runs over a Kai shot at 3.72-4.25 s), _LQ379ZhspI (cyan #00FFFF MrBeast / yellow #FFFF00 Rug; yellow 'LETS GO!' over a MrBeast shot at 23.5-24.0 s), 9L2Yrs6jwb4 (white #FDFDFD host / magenta #F740F8 speaker A / yellow #FAFD08 speaker B; magenta 'SEPTEMBER' at n=396 while speaker A is out of frame), 8-eCvn1gWIg (white lead / pink #FD609C date / yellow #FDDF27 panel; white 'YOURSELF' at 9.52 s and pink 'ALL THE' at 18.38 s both over the wrong shot). Requires diarisation - if diarisation is unavailable, fall back to the single-speaker rule rather than colouring by shot, because colouring by shot is the one thing all four clips prove is wrong.
color_rule.single_speaker: White base (#FFFFFF) plus exactly one accent reserved for a semantic category, not for decoration. uRU9SzlVClg: white for speech, pure red for editor action annotations written in asterisks (*LOOKS AT CHAT*), used only from 2.20-6.05 s, and no frame ever mixes the two. q-SaGj-pDh0: white base with the emphasised word in an accent. -dHfHZgtXJw is the exception - it cycles the whole hue circle per card (green 90-120, cyan 160-180, blue 198-244, violet 264, magenta 294-331, red 2-24, yellow 46-74 deg) purely as decoration, plus one thematic red block for its whole *HANG UP* section.
color_rule.recommended_default: White #FFFFFF speech, red #FF0000 for bracketed non-speech beats (uRU9SzlVClg's exact scheme), upgraded to per-speaker colours when diarisation is present.

outline.recommended: Hard black stroke at ~10% of cap height, plus a soft dark drop shadow.
outline.evidence: Four of seven captioned clips: 8cO8UWyjGyc 10-12 px at 1080 width (~8% of cap height, near-black ring fraction 0.87 out to 10-12 px, soft glow to ~25 px); 9L2Yrs6jwb4 ~10 px (~10% of cap height) plus shadow to ~16 px; 8-eCvn1gWIg ~10 px (~12% of cap height) plus blurred shadow down-right; _LQ379ZhspI ~22 px (~17% of cap height) with rounded joins plus a shadow offset 6-10 px down-right. At a 7.0% cap height on a 1920-tall frame (134 px) that is a 13 px stroke.
outline.alternate_preset_opaque_card: No stroke at all, text sitting on an auto-sized opaque black rounded card with even padding, measured max channel < 28 across the whole card. uRU9SzlVClg only - but uRU9SzlVClg is the single closest structural analogue to the target (locked-off stream, one speaker, two fixed crops), so this is a first-class alternate, not a curiosity.
outline.alternate_preset_neon: Thin bright white inner outline plus a large soft coloured outer glow, no card, no hard black stroke. -dHfHZgtXJw only.

entry_animation.name: centre-anchored per-card scale pop, no undershoot
entry_animation.scope: per card, not per word, and not a full-frame ramp
entry_animation.evidence: Two independent measurements agree to the third decimal. uRU9SzlVClg, measured on 8 separate card starts and identical each time: start 0.909 (range 0.907-0.912), monotonic to peak 1.050 (range 1.047-1.055) at frame +5 = +83 ms, settling at exactly 1.000 by frame +8 = +133 ms, approaching 1.0 from above with no undershoot; bbox centre pinned at (270.0, 76.0) throughout, which is what proves it is a uniform scale about the card centre rather than a per-word width reveal. 8cO8UWyjGyc, measured on the yellow 'SISTER' card at n=223: 0.88x at +2 f, 1.034x at +4, peak 1.055x at +5-6, back to 1.00x by +8 f (0.13 s), with two discriminators against a full-frame ramp - the picture's own push is only 1-2%/s (0.2% over the 0.13 s pop, two orders too small for a 17% swing) and during the 'GIRLFRIEND' card the picture pans ~3.6 px/frame while the caption's centre stays within a few px.

alternate_preset_elastic.name: damped-spring pop with undershoot
alternate_preset_elastic.evidence: 9L2Yrs6jwb4, averaged over 9 cards (per-card starts 0.78-0.88, peaks 1.03-1.07). Start 0.85, crosses 1.0 at 50 ms, peak 1.048 at 83-100 ms, undershoot 0.956 at 183 ms, settled 233-250 ms. The README is right to call this a second preset worth having rather than a correction: its peak time and peak value match the plain pop exactly, it just keeps ringing.

entry_animation.not_supported: Do not blend the six observed behaviours. The full census across seven captioned clips: plain pop peaking ~1.05 at +83 ms (8cO8UWyjGyc, 9L2Yrs6jwb4, uRU9SzlVClg - 3 clips, the only repeated behaviour and the plurality); 1-frame snap 0.84 -> 1.00 with no overshoot in ~33 ms (8-eCvn1gWIg); per-word scale-in 0.34 -> 1.00 over 200-233 ms, anchored bottom-centre, monotonic ease-out (q-SaGj-pDh0); horizontal motion-blur smear-in at full size, resolving over 67-100 ms, with only a +/-2% bloom wobble and no scale ramp (-dHfHZgtXJw); no animation at all, hard swap at full size (_LQ379ZhspI).

highlight_active_word.evidence: highlight_active_word is false in all seven captioned profiles. No reference does karaoke word-highlighting. _LQ379ZhspI states it explicitly ('no per-word karaoke highlight'). At 1-2 words per card there is nothing to highlight.

caption_spec.non_speech_annotations: Write action beats and sound effects in asterisks as their own cards, in the accent colour. uRU9SzlVClg (*LOOKS AT CHAT*, *CHAT SPAMMING AD*, red), -dHfHZgtXJw (*SPINNING*, *HANG UP*, with blinking sparkles), 8-eCvn1gWIg (*BARKS*). Three clips, three source types - this is one of the few things that generalises.
caption_spec.transcription_style: Verbatim including hesitations, with a trailing hyphen on interrupted words (uRU9SzlVClg: 'SO-', 'BEN DA DON-', 'I DONT WANT-'). Do not clean the transcript.

effect_spec: DEFAULT: NO EDITOR-ADDED EFFECTS. This is a measurement, not minimalism. uRU9SzlVClg: 'no editor-added effects at all: no zoom lines, no flash frames, no added emoji or stickers, no meme cutaways, no arrows or circles, no border, no grain, no vignette, no chromatic aberration, no progress bar, no speed ramp'. 8cO8UWyjGyc lists the same absences and calls its speaker-coded pop-in captions 'the only graphic treatment'. The two cleanest references are also two of the three most relevant.

NO IN-SHOT PUSH-IN (push_amount = 0). uRU9SzlVClg holds s=1.0000 with |dx|,|dy| < 0.4 px at every sampled frame from t=0.000 to t=17.100, scale ramp 0.00 %/s, and the punch-in shot is independently locked at s=0.996-1.004. -dHfHZgtXJw measures -0.23 to +1.13 %/s within every shot over spans up to 4.25 s (its one outlier, -3.19 %/s, is a 0.28 s shot where the total change is 0.9%). _LQ379ZhspI is pixel-static on all 11 shots, verified two ways. Three clips, all of them locked-off captures. CONTESTED - see disagreements, because 8cO8UWyjGyc does push.

NO SHAKE (shake_px = 0). Not one of the nine adds synthetic shake. shake_used is true on exactly two profiles - Cfpc04Tpc4k and q-SaGj-pDh0 - and both attribute it to a physical handheld camera in the source, not to an effect. 8-eCvn1gWIg proves absence actively: a +/-12 px translation search returns near-zero error gain on every shot. This is the best-supported single value in the whole spec.
NO SPEED RAMP. speed_ramp_used is false on all nine. The renderer's inability to speed-ramp without audio desync costs nothing.

HARD CUTS, NO TRANSITIONS (default). uRU9SzlVClg and 8cO8UWyjGyc use nothing but hard cuts; _LQ379ZhspI states 'hard cuts only - no transitions of any kind'. -dHfHZgtXJw is the counterexample and puts a blur or flash on every one of its 10 cuts.

OPTIONAL, MAX ONE OR TWO PER CLIP: a red full-frame emphasis flash on the single loudest onset, NOT on a cut. 9L2Yrs6jwb4 measures it exactly: mean R jumps 152 -> 222 in ONE frame while G and B dip, then decays exponentially back to baseline over 19 frames (0.317 s), with identical framing either side - it is an emphasis hit, not an edit. -dHfHZgtXJw fires red flashes at 16.850 s and 22.017 s, both proven to be effects not cuts (ORB s=0.9956/1.0022 with 303 and 151 inliers). 8-eCvn1gWIg ramps a red wash on before a cut and releases it with the cut. q-SaGj-pDh0's green flash at 17.133 s scored MAD 69.4, higher than most of its real cuts, on identical footage.

OPTIONAL: pair the flash with a sub-bass impact. 9L2Yrs6jwb4's 20-60 Hz band jumps from -53/-31 dB to -13 dB at t=6.30 s, co-timed with the red flash. Cfpc04Tpc4k puts a bass-dominated hit on its reveal cut (sub-120 Hz comes within 1.5-2.8 dB of full band, where speech sits 13-29 dB below). Audio-side, so unconstrained by the one-pass video limits.

DO NOT MODEL FLASHES AS A DIP TO #FFFFFF. Cfpc04Tpc4k measured both of its gold light-leak flashes: ~0.30 s total with a ~0.07 s peak, flash A peaking at mean luma 209.5/255, max 235, mean saturation rising 14 -> 71 (a saturated gold that never clips); flash B peaking at mean luma 234.6/255, max 251, saturation collapsing to 1.9 - near-white but still ~4 counts short of pure 255, entering and exiting through orange.

NO GRADE by default. -dHfHZgtXJw is the only reference with a heavy one (crushed blacks, very high saturation, strong sharpening, 'over-processed HDR look') and it is a house style, not a technique the other eight share. If a grade is wanted, a mild contrast/saturation lift is achievable; the crushed-black sharpening halo is not worth chasing.

NO MUSIC BED. Eight of nine have none, each disproved by a measured floor drop: uRU9SzlVClg -47.9 dB RMS at 14.40-14.55 s with -107 dB above 2 kHz; 8cO8UWyjGyc beat autocorrelation 0.044 and 40-300 Hz collapsing 5-7 dB in gaps; 9L2Yrs6jwb4 -42.2 dB in gaps; Cfpc04Tpc4k -77 dBFS windowed RMS; q-SaGj-pDh0 -29.6 dBFS against a -10.3 median; _LQ379ZhspI 20-24 dB band swings. Only 8-eCvn1gWIg (the produced studio piece) has a real bed; -dHfHZgtXJw fades one in only for its last third (40-160 Hz sitting 10-28 dB above the 300 Hz-3 kHz band from ~16.5 s).

NO SFX ON CUTS. 8cO8UWyjGyc: onset strength at cuts sits at only the 84th-93rd percentile, and the clip's largest transient lands 80 ms AFTER the cut, so it is a shout. _LQ379ZhspI: 11.5 dB rise at cuts vs 6.9 dB (sd 4.9) at random times, ~0.9 sd. -dHfHZgtXJw explicitly: 'No sfx stingers on the cuts themselves; the loudness jumps are the incoming shot's own audio.'

OPTIONAL AUDIO DUCK INTO A CUT. -dHfHZgtXJw drops to -54.8 dBFS (digital silence, impossible for live stream audio) for several frames before slamming into the new shot at -12.9 dBFS, at 15.117 s and similarly at 0.350 and 7.717 s. One clip, but it is one of the two most relevant, and it is an audio-graph edit so the video pass is unaffected.
hook_spec: Open cold, mid-sentence, with no title card and no establishing shot - not one of the nine has a title card, and the three most relevant all start mid-utterance. Caption must already be burnt in on the first frame or two: uRU9SzlVClg has 'SO-' up at t=0.05 s, -dHfHZgtXJw has 'CHAT' on frame 1, 8cO8UWyjGyc's frame 0 is already caught mid-pop, _LQ379ZhspI is running by the second frame. Open on a tight rung, not the wide one: -dHfHZgtXJw opens at ~1.40x (f=0.71) with audio at its loudest of the whole clip (-6.8 dBFS RMS in the first 100 ms); _LQ379ZhspI opens at ~1.8x. Land the first cut inside 0.9 s (-dHfHZgtXJw 0.350 s, uRU9SzlVClg 0.650 s, 8cO8UWyjGyc 0.867 s) and make one of the first two shots the shortest in the clip (uRU9SzlVClg's opening 0.65 s shot; 8cO8UWyjGyc's 0.317 s reaction inside the first 1.2 s). Fire 4-5 caption cards in the first 1.8 s (-dHfHZgtXJw: CHAT / LISTEN / THIS / IS A / DREAM; 9L2Yrs6jwb4: nine one-word cards in 2.25 s). The hook device itself is VERBAL, not visual - name a person, pose a question, or promise a thing about to happen; uRU9SzlVClg states this outright ('The hook is purely verbal') and 8cO8UWyjGyc's is a question-plus-reaction beat. Two references use an opening scale ramp instead (_LQ379ZhspI 1.8x -> 1.0x over 0.55 s centre-anchored, 8-eCvn1gWIg a -24% punch-out completed in 0.2 s) and it is renderable as a stepped crop, but neither is a locked-off stream capture, so treat it as optional garnish over the verbal hook rather than a substitute for it.
disagreements: PUSH-IN INSIDE A SHOT - the sharpest conflict in the set, and it splits the three most relevant clips 2-1 against the one the renderer was designed around. ZERO PUSH: uRU9SzlVClg (s=1.0000, |dx|,|dy| < 0.4 px across 17.1 s, 0.00 %/s), -dHfHZgtXJw (-0.23 to +1.13 %/s within every shot), _LQ379ZhspI (all 11 shots pixel-static, ORB returning scale 1.000 dx 0.0 dy 0.0 with 400-1300 inliers), 8-eCvn1gWIg source A (s=1.000, 0.0% error improvement, 'measurably zero push-in'). CONSTANT SLOW PUSH: 8cO8UWyjGyc, +0.8 to +1.2 %/s on EVERY shot, plus a tracking crop pan on 3 of 8. CONSTANT SLOW PULL: 9L2Yrs6jwb4, -2.5 / -3.0 / -3.2 %/s zoom-OUT on three of four shots, which it calls 'close to a house value'. VIOLENT PUSH: 8-eCvn1gWIg source B, +46 %/s over 0.22 s and +12.3 %/s over 1.92 s. There is no consensus value here. push_amount = 0 is kept as the default because it is what the two clips that most resemble the target do, not because it is the majority.

CAPTION VERTICAL POSITION - the three target-relevant clips span 23.5 points of frame height and there is no way to reconcile them. -dHfHZgtXJw 50.0% (measured on five clean cards: 49.72, 50.14, 49.93, 50.03, 50.35, spread 0.6%). 8cO8UWyjGyc 62.5%. uRU9SzlVClg 73.5% (card spanning 69.4-78.5%). The wider set fills the gaps rather than clustering: 9L2Yrs6jwb4 50.2%, 8-eCvn1gWIg 51.1%, q-SaGj-pDh0 52.9%, _LQ379ZhspI 77.9%. The one thing all seven share is being below mid-frame. NOTE: the README's summary list of these positions reads '50.0 / 50.0 / 50.2 / 51.1 / 53 / 62.5 / 73.5' and omits _LQ379ZhspI's own measured 77.9% while adding a second 50.0 - the profile is the authority; the README line appears to have a transcription error. TO SETTLE: measure the target's own facecam head box and the game HUD's top edge and place the text in the widest clear band; there is no reference answer.

CAPTION LEGIBILITY TREATMENT - four ways, and the two most target-relevant clips pick two of the three minority options. Hard black stroke at 8-17% of cap height: 8cO8UWyjGyc (~8%), 9L2Yrs6jwb4 (~10%), 8-eCvn1gWIg (~12%), _LQ379ZhspI (~17%) - four clips, the plurality. Opaque black auto-sized card with no stroke at all: uRU9SzlVClg. Thin white inner outline plus large coloured neon glow: -dHfHZgtXJw. Soft blurred shadow only, no stroke: q-SaGj-pDh0. Both target-analogue clips are outside the plurality, so ship the stroke as the default and the opaque card as a named preset rather than pretending there is one answer.

CAPTION ENTRY ANIMATION - six distinct behaviours over seven captioned clips, enumerated in caption_spec.entry_animation.not_supported. The pop is the plurality at 3 of 7 and it is the only behaviour that repeats, but it is not a majority and the disagreement is real: 8-eCvn1gWIg's 1-frame snap (0.84 -> 1.00 in ~33 ms, no overshoot at all), q-SaGj-pDh0's per-word 0.34 -> 1.00 over 200-233 ms anchored bottom-centre, -dHfHZgtXJw's motion-blur smear at constant 1.00 scale, and _LQ379ZhspI's hard swap are four genuinely different designs, not noise around a mean.

CAPTION COLOUR SEMANTICS - speaker-coded in all four multi-speaker clips (8cO8UWyjGyc, 9L2Yrs6jwb4, _LQ379ZhspI, 8-eCvn1gWIg), each with an off-screen proof; emphasis-coded in the three single-speaker clips (uRU9SzlVClg white/red by category, q-SaGj-pDh0 accent word, -dHfHZgtXJw full hue cycle per card as pure decoration). This is not really a conflict about style, it is a conflict about input: the first behaviour is unreachable without diarisation. Note that -dHfHZgtXJw is the only clip where colour is proven to carry NO information at all - its profile establishes the second party (Ronaldo) never picks up the phone and never speaks.

CAP HEIGHT - 4.0% (q-SaGj-pDh0) to 7.55% (8cO8UWyjGyc), nearly a factor of two, with the two target-relevant clips at the top of the range (7.55%, 7-8%) and the third at 5.8% (uRU9SzlVClg). The 5.8% is partly explained by the opaque card, which buys legibility that a stroke has to buy with size, but that is an inference, not a measurement.

CUT RATE - 0 to 45.3 cuts/min across the nine, and even the eight non-zero ones span 17.2-45.3. The target-relevant three span 24.7-36.1, which is the tightest cluster available but is still a factor of 1.5. jOUyn64mSsk is a genuine single 27.5 s take with no cuts, no captions, no effects and 38.7 M views, which is worth remembering as evidence that the edit is not always what carries a clip.

LADDER TOP END - the tightest rung is 1.38x (8cO8UWyjGyc), ~1.40x (-dHfHZgtXJw), or ~1.5x (_LQ379ZhspI), and uRU9SzlVClg's punch-in could not be pinned at all: its two crops show different parts of the room so they cannot be registered, and a texture-autocorrelation estimate only brackets it at 2-3x. -dHfHZgtXJw's own shot-7 rung carries +/-10% uncertainty because the rotating prize wheel contaminates ORB. Treat f=0.71 as the floor with roughly +/-0.05 of slack.

LOUDNESS - integrated LUFS runs -7.4 (q-SaGj-pDh0) to -23.4 (uRU9SzlVClg) with LRA from 1.7 (_LQ379ZhspI) to 23.9 (jOUyn64mSsk). The target-relevant three alone give -23.4, -19.0 and -13.0. There is no house value here. Four of nine clip at or above 0 dBFS true peak (+1.5, +0.9, +0.3, +0.1) and three sit well below (-9.1, -4.7, -0.2). THE NINE DO NOT SUPPORT A NORMALISATION TARGET. If one is needed, take it from platform guidance, not from these profiles, and say which.

FACECAM-vs-GAMEPLAY SWITCHING CADENCE IS NOT SUPPORTED BY ANY PROFILE. None of the nine contains a gameplay view. 8cO8UWyjGyc is the closest structural match - two windows inside one locked-off source, alternating on the dialogue - but both of its windows contain a person, so nothing here says how long to hold a gameplay crop, when to leave it, or what fraction of the clip should be gameplay. The renderer needs that number and the references cannot give it. TO SETTLE: profile three to five gameplay-stream Shorts the same way, and specifically measure (a) the share of runtime on each of the two windows, (b) whether a switch to gameplay is triggered by the speaker referring to the action or by motion in the gameplay region, and (c) whether the gameplay window ever gets the tightest rung.

THE 0.5-2.0 s SHOT-LENGTH FLOOR IS THINLY EVIDENCED. p10 across the target-relevant three is 0.527 / 0.650 / 0.933 s, so a 0.6 s floor is defensible, but 8cO8UWyjGyc's shortest real shot is 0.317 s and it is deliberate (the front-loaded reaction). Whether sub-0.5 s shots are a hook-only device or usable throughout cannot be settled from three clips.

TYPEFACE IS UNDETERMINED IN EVERY PROFILE. 8cO8UWyjGyc, _LQ379ZhspI and 8-eCvn1gWIg each list it explicitly under 'could not determine'; the rest describe a class ('Anton/Impact-like', 'heavy geometric sans ExtraBold', 'condensed grotesque') without naming it. Any font choice the renderer makes is a substitution, and should be labelled as one. TO SETTLE: render candidate fonts at the measured cap heights and cross-correlate glyph outlines against full-resolution frame crops.

WHETHER -dHfHZgtXJw's SAME-FRAMING CUTS REMOVE SOURCE TIME is undetermined by its own profile (the camera is locked, so framing cannot tell). Its prize-wheel rotation clock bounds the 7.717 s cut at under 0.15 s of removed time; no clock exists at 0.350 or 23.350 s. This matters because it is the difference between a cut and a pure transition effect, and it changes that clip's cut rate.

uRU9SzlVClg's OWN CUT COUNT CARRIES RESIDUAL UNCERTAINTY. Its profile flags 11.717 s as the weakest of nine (head jump small, gift-box clock stepping only 0.24 px, supported by a one-frame shoulder appearance and an I-frame placed one frame later) and notes that if it or 6.700 s is spurious the count drops to 8 and the rate to 28.0 cuts/min.
ffmpeg_notes: FRAMING LADDER -> sendcmd driving crop w/h/x/y. Emit one sendcmd line per cut setting all four at once, then a fixed scale=1080:1920,setsar=1 downstream. The scale output must never change, so the ladder lives entirely in the crop rectangle. Round both crop dimensions to even for H.264 (project gotcha); the <=0.2% aspect drift this introduces disappears in the scale.

SAVED CAMERA RECTS -> compute each rung's (w,h,x,y) once per clip and re-emit byte-identical values on every return to it. 8cO8UWyjGyc returns to a window within 1 px and 0.05% scale and -dHfHZgtXJw returns to exact identity seconds apart; recomputing per shot would introduce a wobble neither reference has.

HARD SWITCH -> a single sendcmd at the cut time. This is a 1:1 match for what the two most relevant references do: uRU9SzlVClg reduces to 'two static crop rectangles, a cut list, and the caption layer', and -dHfHZgtXJw's punch-in is explicitly 'a hard cut to a new crop, never an animated push'.

PUSH-IN -> crop w/h stepped every few frames via sendcmd, or a per-frame expression on crop w/h. Available and correct at +0.8 to +1.2 %/s if 8cO8UWyjGyc's behaviour is wanted, but DEFAULT OFF - see effect_spec and disagreements. Note that stepping crop w without stepping x re-anchors the crop at its top-left; centre-anchored push needs x and y stepped by half the width/height delta in the same command.

TRACKING PAN -> per-frame expression on crop x/y with t available. 8cO8UWyjGyc uses this on 3 of 8 shots (+108 px at +3.3 %/s, -198 px, +754 px following the subject out of the chair). Cheap to add, off by default.
SHAKE -> per-frame expression on crop x/y. Leave at 0: no reference adds it, and 8-eCvn1gWIg actively disproves it with a +/-12 px translation search returning near-zero error gain on every shot.

RED EMPHASIS FLASH -> eq with eval=frame and expressions on gamma_r / gamma_g / gamma_b (all of which accept expressions), one frame at full strength then an exponential decay over ~0.32 s, matching 9L2Yrs6jwb4's measured R 152->222 with G and B dipping and a 19-frame decay. Do NOT implement it as a brightness spike to white.

GOLD LIGHT-LEAK FLASH (Cfpc04Tpc4k) -> PARTLY REPRODUCIBLE. The luma and saturation envelope is an eq brightness + saturation ramp over ~0.30 s with a ~0.07 s peak, capped below clipping (mean luma 209.5, max 235 for the gold one). The streaky vertical banding with the image faintly visible through it is a screen-blended overlay and needs a second filtergraph input - NOT ACHIEVABLE in one pass. Closest substitute: the eq envelope alone, which gets the colour and timing and loses the texture.

WHIP / MOTION-BLUR TRANSITION (-dHfHZgtXJw, 183-217 ms on 6 of its cuts) -> NOT ACHIEVABLE in one pass; directional blur needs tblend/tmix or a boxblur that cannot be time-gated cleanly alongside sendcmd. Closest substitutes, in order: (a) just hard-cut, which is what uRU9SzlVClg, 8cO8UWyjGyc and _LQ379ZhspI do; (b) a 2-3 frame eq brightness dip across the cut, which reads as a beat without pretending to be a blur.
CAPTION POP -> ASS \t transform chain, already implemented in caption_overlays._pop_tags. See implementation_check.

MOTION-BLUR SMEAR CAPTION ENTRY (-dHfHZgtXJw) -> ACHIEVABLE as an approximation: libass supports \blur, so \blur8 with \t(0,100,\blur0) gives a card that resolves from unreadable to sharp over 100 ms at constant scale, which is the measured behaviour minus the horizontal directionality (libass blur is isotropic).
NEON GLOW CAPTION (-dHfHZgtXJw) -> ACHIEVABLE: thin white \3c outline plus a coloured \4c shadow with \blur, no offset. The bloom will be softer than the reference's but the structure matches.

OPAQUE BLACK CARD CAPTION (uRU9SzlVClg) -> ACHIEVABLE via ASS BorderStyle=3 with \bord controlling padding. Caveat: ASS opaque boxes have square corners and the reference's card is rounded, and the box scales with \fscx/\fscy so the pop still applies to card and text together, which is what uRU9SzlVClg measures ('box and text scaling together').

PER-WORD SCALE-IN (q-SaGj-pDh0) -> ACHIEVABLE with per-word spans plus \t, which is already how caption_overlays builds its span list. Anchor is bottom-centre in the reference; ASS scales about the \an alignment point, so this needs \an2-style bottom alignment rather than the \an5 the current prefix uses.
SPEAKER-CODED CAPTION COLOUR -> ASS \c per card, trivial once diarisation supplies the speaker label. The colour is per card, never per shot; see disagreements.
ASS COLOUR FORMAT -> &HAABBGGRR, reversed from hex (project gotcha). The measured colours to convert: #FFFFFF, #FF0000, #FDF400, #F1F6FB, #00FFFF, #FFFF00, #F740F8, #FAFD08, #FD609C, #FDDF27.

CUTAWAY TO EXTERNAL FOOTAGE -> NOT ACHIEVABLE, and not needed. The three target-relevant clips are 100% same-scene reframe. The six references that do cut away (Cfpc04Tpc4k 100% of its cuts, q-SaGj-pDh0 14 of 15, _LQ379ZhspI 8 of 10, 8-eCvn1gWIg 14 of 28, 9L2Yrs6jwb4 1 of 3) are all doing something the renderer structurally cannot. Substitute: a reframe to the other camera window.

COMPOSITED OVERLAYS -> NOT ACHIEVABLE without extra inputs. Specifically ruled out: 9L2Yrs6jwb4's SUBSCRIBE pill + cursor (its profile flags this as the one thing needing a second input), _LQ379ZhspI's circular profile-photo sticker, q-SaGj-pDh0's FIFA trophy PNG and freeze-face emoji, -dHfHZgtXJw's broken-heart sticker and LXST watermark, 8-eCvn1gWIg's branded lockup and channel watermark. PARTIAL SUBSTITUTE: ASS vector drawing (\p1) can render simple shapes in the subtitle pass - q-SaGj-pDh0's drawn red circle annotation and 8-eCvn1gWIg's title lockup are both reachable this way; raster stickers and photos are not.

BACKGROUND REMOVAL (8-eCvn1gWIg's cutout onto a flat grey plate with white outer glow and contact shadow) -> NOT ACHIEVABLE in one pass, and not worth substituting. That clip is a produced studio piece with a second shoot; nothing about it transfers to a locked-off stream VOD.
SPEED RAMP / FREEZE-FRAME (8-eCvn1gWIg's 0.18 s hold) -> NOT ACHIEVABLE without audio desync. No reference speed-ramps, so only the single freeze is lost.

FRAME RATE -> output 60 fps. The target source is 60 fps and the three relevant references are genuine 60 (uRU9SzlVClg mpdecimate keeps 1010/1028, -dHfHZgtXJw 1457/1457, 8cO8UWyjGyc zero exact duplicates). Two references are 30-in-60 containers (Cfpc04Tpc4k 445/836 unique, 8-eCvn1gWIg 48% near-zero diffs in an alternating cadence) - their cut times land on a 30 fps grid and their timings should not be copied frame-for-frame.

FRAME-ACCURATE EXTRACTION -> when verifying a render, use select='eq(n,K)', never 'ffmpeg -ss <t> -i'. Input seeking is not frame-accurate on AV1 and silently returns before/after pairs from the same shot; 8cO8UWyjGyc and q-SaGj-pDh0 both hit this and both flag it.

SELF-VERIFICATION -> scene detection will not see this renderer's own cuts. uRU9SzlVClg's nine cuts produced 2 hits at threshold 0.10 and ZERO at 0.20/0.35; -dHfHZgtXJw's ten produced 6 and ZERO. A locked-off source leaves the background pixel-identical across a jump cut. Verify renders with caption-band-masked per-frame MAD normalised by a local median, and locate the caption band by scanning rather than assuming it - measured bands sat at 40-66%, 45-56.7% and 70.4-77.1% of frame height on different clips.

CAPTION SWAPS WILL LOOK LIKE CUTS to any downstream detector, in the renderer's output as much as in the references. _LQ379ZhspI's threshold-0.10 pass added six false hits that were all caption cards swapping; 8cO8UWyjGyc's added two; q-SaGj-pDh0's added eleven. Mask the band before measuring anything.

caption_overlays._pop_tags.current: POP_START_PCT 91.0 -> POP_PEAK_PCT 105.0 at POP_PEAK_MS 83 -> 100.0 at POP_SETTLE_MS 130, centre-anchored via the \an5 already in the prefix.
caption_overlays._pop_tags.verdict: CORRECT, and better supported than the code comment claims.
caption_overlays._pop_tags.evidence: uRU9SzlVClg measures 0.909 (range 0.907-0.912) -> 1.050 (range 1.047-1.055) at +83 ms -> exactly 1.000 by +133 ms, over 8 separate card starts, with no undershoot and the bbox centre pinned - a direct match to all four constants. 8cO8UWyjGyc independently measures 0.88 at +2 f, peak 1.055 at +5-6 f (83-100 ms), 1.00 by +8 f (133 ms). 9L2Yrs6jwb4 agrees on peak value and peak time (1.048 at 83-100 ms) but keeps ringing to an undershoot of 0.956 at 183 ms before settling at 233-250 ms.
caption_overlays._pop_tags.correction_needed: The source comment in caption_overlays.py credits `_LQ379ZhspI`. That is wrong: `_LQ379ZhspI`'s profile states its cards hard-swap at full size with no visible pop or scale entry at all, and that the only caption scaling in the clip is the opening 0-0.55 s full-frame composite ramp. The measurement belongs to uRU9SzlVClg, corroborated by 8cO8UWyjGyc. The numbers stand; the citation should be repointed.

dynamic_edit.DEFAULT_STYLE.push_amount_0.verdict: CORRECT, on four clips' evidence, but contested by the design reference.
dynamic_edit.DEFAULT_STYLE.push_amount_0.evidence: Supported by uRU9SzlVClg (s=1.0000, 0.00 %/s over 17.1 s), -dHfHZgtXJw (-0.23 to +1.13 %/s within every shot), _LQ379ZhspI (all 11 shots pixel-static, ORB scale 1.000 dx 0.0 dy 0.0 with 400-1300 inliers), 8-eCvn1gWIg source A ('measurably zero push-in'). Contradicted by 8cO8UWyjGyc, which pushes +0.8 to +1.2 %/s on every shot, and by 9L2Yrs6jwb4, which pulls -2.5 to -3.2 %/s. The value is right for the target because the target is a locked-off capture, which is what all four supporting clips are - not because the references agree.

dynamic_edit.DEFAULT_STYLE.shake_px_0.verdict: CORRECT, and this is the best-supported value in the spec.
dynamic_edit.DEFAULT_STYLE.shake_px_0.evidence: shake_used is false on seven of nine profiles. The two that report true - Cfpc04Tpc4k and q-SaGj-pDh0 - both attribute it to a physical handheld camera in the source, not to an added effect, and Cfpc04Tpc4k explicitly warns that a crop-only renderer cannot and should not try to synthesise it. 8-eCvn1gWIg disproves it actively (+/-12 px translation search, near-zero error gain on every shot). No reference adds synthetic shake.

dynamic_edit.DEFAULT_STYLE.snap_amount_0.verdict: CORRECT by default, with one named exception worth exposing.
dynamic_edit.DEFAULT_STYLE.snap_amount_0.evidence: No target-relevant clip snaps: uRU9SzlVClg, -dHfHZgtXJw and 8cO8UWyjGyc all change framing by hard cut only. The exception is an OPENING snap, not a per-shot one: _LQ379ZhspI ramps 1.8x -> 1.0x over the first 0.55 s (measured via caption cap height at 1.58 / 1.45 / 1.32 / 1.15 / 1.12 / 1.00x) and 8-eCvn1gWIg snaps out -24% in 0.2 s (0.81x by k6, 0.76x by k12). Both are hook devices on the first shot. If snap is exposed at all, gate it to t < 0.6 s.

dynamic_edit.DEFAULT_STYLE.timing.evidence: target_shot_s = 1.25 and max_shot_s = 2.40 are faster than any of the three target-relevant clips: their avg_shot_s are 1.454 (8cO8UWyjGyc), 1.713 (uRU9SzlVClg) and 2.208 (-dHfHZgtXJw), and their p90 shot lengths are 2.95, 2.66 and 3.633 s. The code comment cites '31-47 cuts/min' from the superseded mechanical table; the measured target-relevant band is 24.7-36.1. Suggest target_shot_s 1.8 and max_shot_s 3.0; min_shot_s 0.60 is well placed against p10 values of 0.527 / 0.650 / 0.933.
